c.tagline: A honey-colored desert city of windcatchers, mud-brick alleys and living Zoroastrian tradition.

taxi.fareNote: Foreign bank and credit cards do NOT work anywhere in Iran — bring cash (USD or EUR) to exchange for rials and carry plenty. Agree the fare before getting in a street taxi, or use the Snapp/Tapsi apps, which are cheaper and priced automatically.

emergency.note: 110 reaches police and 115 is the ambulance/emergency medical line; English is limited, so ask your hotel to help if possible.

avoid.reason: Nothing serious beyond occasional taxi overcharging and motorbikes in the old town's narrow lanes.

hood_desc: The oldest quarter of Yazd, a UNESCO-listed labyrinth of mud-brick alleys, courtyard houses and wind towers around the Fahadan Museum and the 12-Imam shrine; the most atmospheric place to stay, in a restored traditional hotel. Best for soaking up the old city on foot.

The city's landmark public square, dominated by the towering three-story Amir Chakhmaq façade and its rows of arched alcoves, ringed by teahouses, a bazaar and a confectionery district; a central, lively base a short walk from most sights.

The commercial heart around the Jameh Mosque and the covered Grand Bazaar, where lanes of coppersmiths, textile and sweet shops thread between historic caravanserais; the best area for markets and everyday shopping.

A quieter district built around the Dowlatabad Garden, a Persian paradise garden with the tallest windcatcher in the world and reflecting pools; leafy, calm and residential, a little removed from the tourist core.
Yazd's modern hotel and dining strip southeast of the old city, with newer four-star hotels, cafes and easy road access; convenient and comfortable, though it lacks the old-town character.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated but brackish and mineral-heavy; most visitors drink bottled.

transit.hours: City buses run roughly 6:00 AM to 9:00 PM; there is no metro, so shared and app taxis fill the gaps and cover evenings.
transit.note: Yazd has no metro or tram; getting around is by city bus, cheap shared 'savari' taxis on fixed routes, private taxis and the Snapp/Tapsi ride apps. The compact old city is best explored on foot.
transit.pay: Buses use a rechargeable smart card bought at kiosks; taxis are paid in cash rial (foreign cards don't work). Ride-app fares can be paid in cash to the driver.

bus: Intercity VIP coaches to Isfahan, Shiraz, Tehran and Kerman
train: Yazd railway station on the Tehran-Kerman/Bandar Abbas line (trains to Tehran, Isfahan, Kerman)

transit.m: Snapp or Tapsi ride-hail app to the old city (~15 min)
Airport taxi to the center (~15-20 min); agree the fare first

tip.r: Not obligatory; rounding up or leaving small change for good service is appreciated. Taarof (polite refusal) is common — offer anyway.
